newsitem.title: USA: Senators introduce bill to reform U.S. statistics.
newsitem.headline: Senators introduce bill to reform U.S. statistics.

text.p: Two Democratic U.S. Senators, Daniel Patrick Moynihan and Bob Kerrey, have introduced a bill to require a study on reform of the nation's statistical system.

Moynihan, who represents New York, and Kerrey, of Nebraska, said they were seeking to respond to concerns that the statistical system is not well coordinated and that the data itself has not been adapted to reflect the changing nature of the economy.

"It is clear that to preserve and improve the statistical system we must consider reforming it, yet we must not attempt to reform the system until we have heard from experts in the field," the senators said in a joint statement.
The legislation would establish a 13-member panel of experts from a variety of backgrounds to examine various aspects of the system, such as whether it could be improved through a centralized agency.
Moynihan and Kerrey also said they received a letter from nine former chairmen of the Council of Economic Advisers backing the legislation.
Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, who served on the Council under President Ford, was among the backers.
